previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with unresectable extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and recent history of GNR bacteremia and C. difficile infection, was admitted with a two-week cough, two days of fatigue, and a one-day history of low-grade fever up to 101°F. He was evaluated for possible cholangitis given his elevated bilirubin and history of biliary stents. CT imaging suggested partial obstruction of the left biliary stent, but he defervesced without intervention, and liver tests normalized. Blood cultures remained negative at 72 hours, respiratory viral panel was negative, and no evidence of colitis was found. His leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were likely due to chemotherapy or a viral illness. He improved clinically and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with oncology for CBC monitoring and ongoing cancer care.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen pelvis dated ___ and ___, and abdominal ultrasound dated ___.  

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.  

FINDINGS:

This exam is limited for assessment of the midline structures due to overlying
bowel gas.  Allowing for this limitation, the liver appears enlarged,
unchanged from prior exams, without evidence of focal lesions.  There is
moderate central intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  Allowing for
differences in modality, the degree of intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation
is grossly unchanged from the CT of the abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

The patient is status post common bile duct stenting, with a stent seen in the
appropriate position and expected pneumobilia. The gallbladder demonstrates
wall thickening, measuring 7mm (previously 1.1 cm),  without hydropic changes.
There is sludge within the gallbladder. 

Limited views of the pancreatic body are unremarkable. The pancreatic head and
tail are obscured by overlying bowel gas. Doppler assessment of the main
portal vein shows patency and normal hepatopetal flow.  

The spleen is enlarged, measuring 17.6 cm.  

The right and left kidneys are unremarkable without evidence of stones,
hydronephrosis, or masses.  The right kidney measures 12.3 cm, and the left
kidney measures 12.9 cm. 

Limited views of the aorta and IVC are unremarkable.  There is no ascites. 
There is a small right-sided pleural effusion.  

IMPRESSION:

1. Status post common bile duct stenting with expected pneumobilia. Moderate
central intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Allowing for differences in
modality, the degree of intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation is grossly
unchanged from the CT of the abdomen and pelvis dated ___.   

2.  Gallbladder sludge. Slight interval decrease in the degree of gallbladder
wall thickening, without hydropic changes.  

3.  Stable splenomegaly.
